newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent crude softer as May expires.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent crude softer as May expires.

text.p: SIMEX Brent crude was softer on Tuesday as the prompt month of May expires, brokers said.

The market also discounted further impact of a report that U.S. and Saudi intelligence authorities have linked a senior Iranian government official to a group suspected of bombing a U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia last year.
The market kept their eyes peeled on the Washington Post report which caused Brent to firm in London on Monday, as well as a rally on NYMEX unleaded gasoline ahead of the U.S. driving season.
May was traded on the back of the spread, with an offer heard at $18.08 a barrel, down from London's close on Monday at $18.19.
June last traded at $18.27 a barrel, down seven cents from London's $18.34-close. Brokers said June was seeing good buying support at the $18.25/$18.26 level.
NYMEX crude on ACCESS traded slightly higher at $19.91 per barrel, up one cent from New York.
